parsed.explanation: No trans-specific data exists: no record of police targeting of gender-nonconforming people, no facility, custody, hospital-ward, document or border rules, and no trans violence figures. The one documented legal fact is an inherited same-sex conduct offence (max 14 years) that reporting across 2010–2013 and an advocacy assessment describe as unenforced, with no arrests or prosecutions — a latent lever, not an active trans-facing restriction, and sexuality law is secondary here. Against that: no anti-discrimination protection covers gender identity, reform has been repeatedly rejected, and senior officials have publicly attacked LGBT recognition, so the climate signal is hostile. Institutionally the record shows corruption, lengthy pretrial detention and thin recourse. Per the rule that a latent tangential statute plus open questions plus thin recourse sits one step below the acceptance-with-protections tier, and absent any documented acceptance to offset it, I place this in the Elevated band, lower-middle.
